vars.description: Looking at .md files in this repo, what is a word that some contain and some do not -- aim for around '50%'? Consider tracked and non-ignored untracked files across the whole repository, even when run from a subdirectory. Handle no qualifying word gracefully.
vars.os_info: Debian Linux with Python 3 and Git installed
vars.review: Use per-file word presence; choose closest frequency to half, excluding words in every file. Include repository Markdown files only. Prefer readable code.
vars.example:
command python3 -c 'import subprocess,pathlib,re,collections,os; root=pathlib.Path(subprocess.check_output(["git","rev-parse","--show-toplevel"],text=True).strip()); names=subprocess.check_output(["git","-C",str(root),"ls-files","-z","--cached","--others","--exclude-standard","--","*.md"]).split(b"\0"); files=[root/os.fsdecode(n) for n in set(names) if n]; counts=collections.Counter(); [counts.update(set(re.findall("[a-z]+",p.read_text().lower()))) for p in files]; n=len(files); candidates=[w for w,c in counts.items() if 0<c<n]; word=min(candidates,key=lambda w:(abs(2*counts[w]-n),w)) if candidates else None; print(f"{word}: {counts[word]}/{n}" if word else "No qualifying word")'
##DANGERLEVEL=0## Reads repository Markdown files.
